actions.action: Check soil conditions and adjust watering (water deeply, avoid waterlogging)
Fertilize in spring with an azalea food such as Espoma Azalea-Tone
Ensure the azalea is in well-drained acidic soil (amend or replant if needed)
Site the plant for morning sun and afternoon shade in a protected spot
Apply 2–3 inches of mulch around the root zone
Add wind protection in colder areas
If discoloration comes with leaf drop, stunting or spotting, inspect for pests, root issues or nutritional imbalances
Check the hardiness range for your variety and choose cold-tolerant varieties

verdict.reason: The answer mainly frames red winter leaves as normal seasonal color, mentioning stress only as a secondary possibility, and buries the watering and fertilizing fix among marketing and general care tips. It does not discourage the needed care, so it is not harmful.
